issues_detected.description: Deidentification is described two incompatible ways. is_deidentified.method records the type as 'NoDeIdentification' with the explanation that 'no identifiers were collected, so no active de-identification was necessary', while participant_privacy.anonymization_method states that 'Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule was removed from the public release via the Safe Harbor method' and is_deidentified.identifiers_removed enumerates removed PHI, sex, race/ethnicity and medications. Removal of PHI by Safe Harbor is an active de-identification step and contradicts the claim that none was necessary. The record does not flag this pair as a source conflict, unlike the six conflicts it does surface in source_caveats.
issues_detected.recommendation: Reconcile the two statements or record them as an explicit source disagreement in is_deidentified, e.g. state that no direct identifiers were collected at capture AND that a Safe Harbor review plus removal of sex/race/medications was applied before public release.

issues_detected.description: No software is named that produced or transformed the released data. preprocessing_strategies describes format conversions (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, .FIT and .csv to Open mHealth, .xml to WFDB, REDCap to OMOP CDM) and states only that processing moved to 'a combination of automated and custom processing'; no converter, mapper or pipeline is named or versioned. The software that is named fills other roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application capture data, FAIRhub and Microsoft Azure host it, and the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard validates it.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the conversion and mapping tools (and versions or repository tags) used for .fda/.sdt to DICOM, .FIT/.csv to Open mHealth, .xml to WFDB and REDCap to OMOP, ideally linking the specific AI-READI GitHub repositories rather than the organization root.

issues_detected.description: There is no download_url field. The access route is documented only indirectly, through page (https://fairhub.io/datasets/3) and data_governance.access_review_process, which names https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access and the login, attestation and licence steps.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate download_url with https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access so machine consumers can resolve the access endpoint without parsing governance prose.

issues_detected.description: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is set to 'restricted' although the underlying sources give 'HL7:2N (normal)' and an accessType of 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired'. The record discloses this as its own enum mapping in source_caveats, so the value is traceable, but a consumer filtering on the enum will see a stricter classification than either source states.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the caveat but consider a value nearer the sources' meaning (publicly downloadable subject to attestation and licence) or add the raw source values as structured fields alongside the enum.

issues_detected.description: No data protection impact assessment exists: notes record that 'no data protection impact analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted'. The cross-field expectation that a DPIA accompany an assessed re-identification risk is therefore unmet, although participant_privacy.reidentification_risk is assessed and mitigations (dissemination system, licence, watermarking) are described.
issues_detected.recommendation: Conduct and record a DPIA, or state explicitly in a data_protection_impacts entry why one was judged unnecessary given the Safe Harbor release.

issues_detected.description: No future_use_impacts entry (rai:dataSocialImpact) is present. Anticipated downstream social impact is addressed only obliquely, through the disparity-reduction rationale for the recommended splits, the watermarking and licence rationale, and the ELSI and Community Advisory Board review recorded in ethical_reviews.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add future_use_impacts entries describing anticipated downstream social impacts of models trained on the data and the mitigations already in place.

issues_detected.description: data_governance names a committee ('AI-READI Consortium') and an accountable organization but carries no committee_contact. Contact points exist elsewhere: hsdrely@uw.edu in ethical_reviews and contact@aireadi.org plus https://aireadi.org/contact in maintainers.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate data_governance.committee_contact with the Data Access Committee or consortium governance address.

issues_detected.description: The institution accountable for the dataset is contested between Washington University in St. Louis (FAIRhub managing organization, lead sponsor, licence Licensor) and the University of Washington (IRB, principal investigator, NIH RePORTER awardee). creators.affiliations lists both. The record surfaces the conflict in creators.source_caveats, data_governance.source_caveats and top-level source_caveats rather than resolving it, which is appropriate handling but leaves the accountable party ambiguous for a reuser.
issues_detected.recommendation: Retain the caveat and, if possible, add a resolving statement from the consortium about which institution is accountable for the released artifact.

issues_detected.description: The size of the longitudinal follow-up arm is given as approximately 4% (FAIRhub healthsheet) in relationships and collection_timeframes and as 10% (FAIRhub README, RO-Crate, NIH RePORTER) in the same fields. Both are carried rather than merged, with the tier tie explained.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change required to the datasheet's handling; upstream sources should be reconciled.

issues_detected.description: sensitive_elements_present is false and confidential_elements_present is false for a clinical dataset carrying laboratory values, retinal imaging, continuous glucose traces and in-home environmental sensing. The claim is defensible only because sex, race/ethnicity, medications and PHI were moved to the controlled-access counterpart, and the record says so explicitly; a reader who reads the flag alone could nonetheless underestimate the health-data sensitivity of what remains.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the flags but add a sentence noting that the release still comprises individual-level clinical and physiological measurements, whose reuse is governed by the licence.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3 is well formed and the 10.60775 prefix is the FAIRhub DataCite prefix, consistent with publisher https://fairhub.io/ and page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; id repeats the same DOI as a URI.

All three NIH awards follow valid activity-code patterns for their stated agency: OT2OD032644 (OT2 Other Transaction, Office of the Director, consistent with the Common Fund Bridge2AI programme), P30DK035816 (NIDDK centre grant) and UL1TR003096 (NCATS CTSA), and OT2OD032644 is linked to its RePORTER project record.

The file inventory is internally exact: the nine file_collections plus the root metadata directory sum to 356,343 files, matching total_file_count exactly, and their byte counts sum to 3,815,969,360,064 against a stated total_size_bytes of 3,815,969,779,678, the 419,614-byte remainder being the unsized root metadata files.

Every cohort count reconciles. Race/ethnicity (380+545+519+836), sex (951+1,329) and diabetes status (776+560+686+258) each sum to 2,280, the split sizes (1,576+352+352) sum to 2,280, and each split's internal race, sex and diabetes breakdowns sum both across strata and down to the whole-cohort totals.

Human-subjects logic is satisfied end to end: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by IRB protocol STUDY00016228 with an approval date and named reviewing body, by reliance agreements for the two other sites, and by a detailed informed_consent block with consent type, scope, documentation and withdrawal mechanism.

Temporal ordering is coherent: IRB approval 2022-12-20 precedes the 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 collection window, which precedes the 2025-11-17 issue date, and the three release dates (2024-05-03, 2024-11-08, 2025-11-17) ascend with participant counts 204, 1,067, 2,280.

Format claims are consistent across levels: distribution_formats (DICOM, CSV, JSON, Markdown with MIME types) matches the per-collection conforms_to_standard declarations (WFDB, OMOP CDM, DICOM, Open mHealth, ESDS, all under CDS v0.1.1) and the format-by-modality account in the description.

The record distinguishes the public release from the controlled-access counterpart throughout — description, sensitive_elements, known_limitations, data_governance — and states plainly that the controlled version 'is not the artifact this record describes', which keeps the scope claims semantically clean.

Six source disagreements are declared rather than silently resolved, each with its tier reasoning (acronym expansion, accountable institution, target enrolment, enrolment start date, longitudinal arm size, pilot-versus-year-two framing), which is unusually disciplined provenance handling.

Absence statements are affirmative rather than empty: no imputation was performed, no erratum exists, no labelling was performed because the dataset is hypothesis agnostic, no DPIA was conducted, and no external audit was performed — each recorded as a finding rather than left blank.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; prior versions 10.60775/fairhub.1 and 10.60775/fairhub.2
sub_elements.quality_note: A resolvable DOI is given, repeated as the record id, and the version series is DOI-addressed, so any specific release can be cited unambiguously.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Matches 10.XXXXX/... ; prefix 10.60775 is FAIRhub's DataCite prefix and agrees with publisher https://fairhub.io/ and page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3. No RRID is claimed; ROR IDs (e.g. ROR:00cvxb145) and an ORCID for the PI are well formed.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description of roughly 2,000 characters naming 2,280 participants, the 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 window, three sites, the nine data types with their formats, 356,343 files and 3.82 TB, plus the boundary against the controlled-access version
sub_elements.quality_note: Far beyond the 200-character threshold and specific throughout: cohort size, sites, modalities, standards, scale and scope exclusions are all stated rather than gestured at.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Description is internally consistent with instances.counts (2,280), collection_timeframes, total_file_count and total_size_bytes; the T2DM/salutogenesis framing matches purposes and tasks.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [Diabetes mellitus, Type 2 Diabetes, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam, Data Sharing, Exploratory Data Collection]
sub_elements.quality_note: Ten keywords spanning condition, method and modality; a reader searching on either the disease or any single modality would find the record.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Every keyword is substantiated elsewhere in the record (ECG in cardiac_ecg, CGM in wearable_blood_glucose, retinal imaging across four collections).

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; ten file_collections with ids of the form https://fairhub.io/datasets/3#retinal_oct, each with path, description, file_count, total_bytes and conforms_to
sub_elements.quality_note: A landing page plus a genuinely hierarchical resource inventory: datatype, modality, device and participant nesting is described and each collection is separately addressable and sized.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Collection ids are fragment identifiers under the landing page URL, so the hierarchy is resolvable; file counts sum exactly to total_file_count.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: relationship_type is_new_version_of -> doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.1; relationships entries describing participant-level linkage across the nine datatype directories
sub_elements.quality_note: Typed version lineage to both predecessors, plus an explicit statement of how records for one person are linked across directories by study ID.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The two targets match the DOIs and dates given in distribution_dates and version_access, so the lineage is self-consistent.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'The AI-READI custom data license version 2.0, published at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036 and naming Washington University in St. Louis as Licensor...'; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research; ip_restrictions.restrictions: 'Title to the data, and all industrial and intellectual property rights in it, remain solely and exclusively with the licensor...'
sub_elements.quality_note: Access policy is stated at operational depth: storage confined to institutional servers or BAA-covered cloud, derivative and synthetic data inherit the terms, automatic termination on breach, indemnification, and a separate carve-out that the docs.aireadi.org documentation is CC-BY 4.0.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Licence DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17555036 uses the Zenodo prefix correctly. The disease_specific_research permission is consistent with intended_uses.usage_notes and with the access attestation described in data_governance.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions listing NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy security best practices; other_compliance: 'not an FDA-regulated drug study and not an FDA-regulated device study'; human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance naming HIPAA Safe Harbor and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048
sub_elements.quality_note: Confidentiality classification, HIPAA status, the applicable NIH policy and the FDA determination are all stated, and the record explains how it derived the enum value rather than asserting it.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Registered warning: 'restricted' is the record's own mapping of 'HL7:2N (normal)' and 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired', disclosed in source_caveats. data_governance.committee_contact is absent, though hsdrely@uw.edu and contact@aireadi.org appear in ethical_reviews and maintainers; the shortfall is a slot, not the information.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; data_governance.access_review_process: 'The access route for version 3.0.0 is the FAIRhub access page at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access', with the steps of verified-ID login, T2DM-research attestation and licence acceptance; third_party_sharing.is_shared: true
sub_elements.quality_note: The platform link and the exact access procedure are both given, including what the requester must agree to and how the controlled-access route differs. Scored on the sub-element's 'platform access instructions' clause.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Flagged as a completeness issue: the dedicated download_url field is empty, so the endpoint is only reachable by reading governance prose.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: DICOM (application/dicom), CSV (text/csv), JSON (application/json), Markdown (text/markdown), each with notes on which directories use it; per-collection conforms_to_standard values WFDB, OMOP_CDM, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, CDS
sub_elements.quality_note: Formats are given with MIME types and mapped onto the specific directories that carry them, so a consumer knows what tooling each part of the release needs.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The format-to-directory mapping agrees with the description and with each file_collection's conforms_to. Character encoding is not stated anywhere, a minor gap for the text formats.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: two is_new_version_of links; external_resources: https://docs.aireadi.org/, https://aireadi.org/ and subpages, https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, https://github.com/AI-READI, https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x, https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449, https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation site, project site, code and guideline repositories, two peer-reviewed publications with DOIs and the CDS specification are all linked, each with a note explaining what it contains and its licence where relevant.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Publication DOIs use valid Nature (10.1038) and BMJ (10.1136) prefixes; all URLs are structurally sound and on plausible domains.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on E2 evidence: distribution_formats populated (DICOM/CSV/JSON/Markdown), page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 with an access page, third_party_sharing.is_shared true, and a licence that expressly grants reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms: 'grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to download, reproduce and use the data and to create derivative works for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes'; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research
sub_elements.quality_note: Reuse is permitted and the boundaries are explicit — what may be redistributed, what may be published as figures, how models trained on the data may be released, and what happens on termination.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The custom licence is restrictive relative to CC-BY but unambiguously permits reuse; its restrictions are echoed consistently in prohibited_uses and intended_uses rather than contradicting them.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence from E2: distribution_formats and an accessible landing/access page.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to describing CDS v0.1.1 layout with WFDB for ECG, OMOP CDM for clinical tables, DICOM for FLIO/OCT/OCTA/photography, Open mHealth for wearables and NASA ESDS ASCII for environmental data; distribution_formats with media types
sub_elements.quality_note: Every modality is expressed in an established domain standard rather than an ad hoc layout, which is precisely what makes the release integrable with other clinical and imaging corpora.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Standards are appropriate to their data types (WFDB for waveforms, DICOM for ophthalmic imaging, OMOP for observational clinical tables). Character encoding is never stated, the only element of this sub-element left open.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence from E2.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: [CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; per-collection conforms_to statements
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is asserted at three levels — the datasheet's own schema, the dataset's directory specification, and the file standard within each collection — and the CDS specification is linked in external_resources.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: OMOP CDM conformance is corroborated by the clinical_data collection's one-to-one CSV-to-OMOP-table mapping and the dqd_omop.json quality dashboard file; the claims are substantiated rather than nominal.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence from E2.
sub_elements.evidence: variables: about 40 entries, e.g. variable_name hba1c (float, '%', 'Whole blood assay performed by the University of Washington Nutrition and Obesity Research Center', reference range 4.0-6.0); moca_total_score with maximum_value 30.0 and interpretation thresholds; monofilament_response categorical with categories; ldl_cholesterol_calculated with derivation
sub_elements.quality_note: A real data dictionary: names, types, units, measurement technique, reference ranges, derivations and interpretation guidance, plus participants.json/participants.tsv shipped in the release.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Units and types are appropriate throughout (HbA1c in %, troponin in ng/L, logMAR acuity, log CS). Identifiers are local names rather than ontology terms such as LOINC codes, though OMOP conformance supplies standard concepts for the clinical tables. One honest simplification is declared: eleven spectral channels are collapsed into a single array variable because the sources do not name them.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: three categories with examples (multimodal model development, pseudotime manifold analysis, methodological reuse of the blueprint); prohibited_uses: six, including clinical treatment decisions, re-identification attempts, sharing with third-party model vendors for training, and removal of watermarking; discouraged_uses: two, on representativeness and interim releases
sub_elements.quality_note: All three registers are populated with reasoned, dataset-specific guidance; the prohibition on model-vendor training and the five-figure publication limit are concrete enough to act on.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Guidance is consistent with the licence text and with the known_biases and known_limitations entries it draws on; the discouraged use about representativeness matches sampling_strategies.why_not_representative.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1 and E8 evidence: description states '2,280 participants with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus' who 'completed pre-visit questionnaires, a single on-site visit'; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes REDCap recruitment, screening and electronic consent. The governance condition is independently met by regulatory_restrictions (E2), which imposes NIH GDS security obligations.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews[0]: 'University of Washington Institutional Review Board, Human Subjects Division ... approved under IRB protocol STUDY00016228. The initial approval ... was received on 20 December 2022'; reliance agreements with UAB and UCSD; ethical_reviews[1] naming the ELSI reviewers Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman and Nicholas Evans; ethical_reviews[2] describing an eleven-member Community Advisory Board
sub_elements.quality_note: Oversight is documented as a structure, not a checkbox: protocol number, approval date, published approval letter, reliance arrangements, annual renewal obligation, named bioethics reviewers and a community board that reviewed the consent form.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by irb_approval and a named ethics_review_board. A conflict over the reviewing body's name ('Washington University IRB' in the RO-Crate against a Seattle UW address) is disclosed as a source caveat. Data protection impact is a documented absence — notes state no DPIA has been conducted — which is recorded rather than concealed.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human-subjects evidence from E1/E8, and independently the E2 governance constraint (NIH GDS security standards, HIPAA compliance status).
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.method: de-identification type 'NoDeIdentification' with the explanation that 'no identifiers were collected ... but that the team checked that no identifiable data per US HIPAA were present'; identifiers_removed: 'Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule; information related to the sex and race/ethnicity of participants; medications used'; deidentification_details recording confidentiality level 'HL7:2N (normal)' and internal-only review
sub_elements.quality_note: Method, removed identifiers, the techniques not used (date shifting, k-anonymity), the review process and the absence of an external audit are all stated, which is enough for a reuser to judge the residual risk.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency check FAILS on the method statement: 'no active de-identification was necessary' contradicts participant_privacy's Safe Harbor removal of PHI and the identifiers_removed list. The point is still earned because the substance a reuser needs is present and specific; the defect is that two descriptions coexist unreconciled. Also noted: the healthsheet's question on post-de-identification re-identification measures is recorded as left blank.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1 description ('2,280 participants') and E8 collection_mechanisms (recruitment, consent and in-home device placement with participants). Not asserted from E4's own fields, and not from the governance structure, which does not reach this sub-element.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy.privacy_techniques: the environmental sensor and Garmin tracker 'do not capture video or audio, are not equipped with GPS location monitoring, and are not synced with participant-owned devices'; watermarking such that 'licensees must not remove, obscure, alter or mask the watermarking'; results returned by HIPAA-compliant encrypted email; reidentification_risk: 'a theoretical risk of future re-identification. AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics and could facilitate individual-level identification'
sub_elements.quality_note: Risk is assessed rather than asserted away, and each protection is tied to the risk it addresses — device selection to collection risk, watermarking and licence to redistribution risk, controlled access to the sensitive variables.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The stated risk is plausible and appropriate for multimodal imaging and continuous physiological data, where fully anonymous release is not achievable; the mitigation set matches the risk described. participant_privacy.data_linkage discloses the participant-ID folder naming and participants.tsv.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human-subjects evidence from E1 description and E8 collection_mechanisms.
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type: 'Written informed consent, obtained for most participants remotely as electronic consent through REDCap ... and otherwise in person'; consent_scope covering open-source repository placement and biospecimen use; withdrawal_mechanism: 'Participants were permitted to withdraw consent at any time ... any data that had been shared or used up to that point would remain in the dataset'; consent_documentation: the UW consent form distributed as a PDF with version 3.0.0
sub_elements.quality_note: Type, scope, documentation, withdrawal semantics and site-level variation under IRB reliance are all covered, and the honest limit of withdrawal (already-released data remain) is stated as it is stated to participants.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency check passes: IRB approval and consent procedures are both documented, as expected when involves_human_subjects is true. consent_scope's note that the public version is limited to T2DM research matches license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission and the access attestation.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human-subjects evidence from E1 description and E8 collection_mechanisms.
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: false with special_protections: 'Minors are not enrolled ... Pregnancy and gestational diabetes are exclusion criteria ... Prisoners are not a target population'; participant_compensation: 200 US dollars, paid after device return, 'not prorated', plus parking, transit and rideshare cost coverage
sub_elements.quality_note: The negative finding on vulnerable populations is substantiated by the eligibility rules that produce it rather than merely flagged false, and compensation is given with amount, timing, rationale and funding source.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Coherent with human_subject_research.special_populations ('No protected population is targeted ... adults aged 40 years and older') and with the age subpopulation. The caveat that the stipend may change in later years with IRB notification is disclosed.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations: four entries — race/ethnicity (Hispanic 380, Asian 545, Black 519, White 836), biological sex (951 male, 1,329 female), diabetes status (no diabetes 776, lifestyle 560, oral 686, insulin 258) and age (mean 60.8, SD 11.3, eligibility 40-85)
sub_elements.quality_note: Distributions are given at cohort and split level with exact counts, and the record explains that race and sex are published only as aggregates because the variables themselves are under controlled access.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All four distributions sum to 2,280, matching instances.counts. subpopulation_elements_present is false for race and sex and true for diabetes and age, which correctly encodes what is released rather than what was measured; the apparent tension with the healthsheet's 'No' answer is explained in source_caveats.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances.counts: 2280 with instance_type 'individual study participant'; total_file_count: 356343; total_size_bytes: 3815969779678; splits: 1,576 / 352 / 352 train/validation/test; per-collection file_count values
sub_elements.quality_note: Counts are reported at participant, file, byte and split level, and per data collection, so a user can size any subset before downloading.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Arithmetic verified: collection file counts sum exactly to 356,343 and collection bytes sum to within 419,614 of total_size_bytes (the unsized root metadata files); split sizes sum to 2,280.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
sub_elements.evidence: variables: ~40 typed entries with units and measurement techniques; is_tabular: false; splits.split_details describing the 70/15/15 recommended split with per-stratum counts and the participants.tsv assignment; subpopulations carrying subpopulation_elements_present flags
sub_elements.quality_note: The split is not merely announced but published with the assignment shipped in participants.tsv, its balancing rationale explained, and the demographic composition of each partition tabulated.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: is_tabular=false is right for a release dominated by DICOM, WFDB and JSON, even though the clinical_data collection is tabular OMOP CSV. The split flags and subpopulation flags are used distinctly and the split arithmetic reconciles in every stratum.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances.data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:43; instances.notes: 'Each instance consists of all of the data available for one individual ... spanning survey data, clinical data, retinal imaging data, environmental sensor data, continuous glucose monitor data and wearable activity monitor data ... there is no unstructured text data'; diabetes severity strata in subpopulations
sub_elements.quality_note: The condition (T2DM across four severity strata), the covered domains and the explicitly absent modality (free text) are all stated, with a coded topic identifier.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The topic coding and modality list agree with the description, file_collections and variables; the negative claim about unstructured text is consistent with raw_sources, which cites free-text fields as a reason the raw data are not released.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: six entries, e.g. 'The Garmin Vivosmart 5 had to be charged every two to three days, so there are gaps in the activity monitoring record' and the FLIO entry on movement tolerance and unsubtractable background photons; sampling_strategies with is_random false and why_not_representative; missing_data_documentation with patterns, causes and handling_strategy
sub_elements.quality_note: Anomalies are modality-specific and mechanistic, naming the device behaviour that produces each artefact, which is far more useful than a generic quality caveat.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: missing_data_documentation's statement that 'No imputation of missing values is reported for the released dataset' is an affirmative absence and is consistent with the empty imputation_protocols concept in E8. The anomalies align with known_limitations.coverage_limitation.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on E2 evidence: distribution_formats populated, page and access page resolvable, third_party_sharing.is_shared true.
sub_elements.evidence: version: 3.0.0; description and citation both name version 3.0.0; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3
sub_elements.quality_note: A semantic version is given and is consistent everywhere it recurs, including the DOI suffix series.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: 3.0.0 is well formed; the major-version increments across releases match the substantive cohort expansions described in distribution_dates.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence from E2.
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.versions_available listing 1.0.0 (10.60775/fairhub.1, 3 May 2024, 204 participants), 2.0.0 (10.60775/fairhub.2, 8 November 2024, 1,067 participants, 'no longer accessible') and 3.0.0; version_details naming per-version documentation and healthsheets at https://docs.aireadi.org/docs/1/dataset/healthsheet and .../docs/2/...
sub_elements.quality_note: Each version is addressable by DOI, has matching documentation and a matching healthsheet, and the support policy is stated plainly: older versions are not supported and 2.0.0 is no longer accessible.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The version list, distribution_dates and related_datasets agree on DOIs, dates and participant counts. The existence of a 'mini version' of 3.0.0 for pipeline development is also recorded.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence from E2.
sub_elements.evidence: updates.update_details: 'Changes between versions are described in the CHANGELOG file included in the dataset and visible at docs.aireadi.org'; file_collections root-metadata entry listing CHANGELOG.md; distribution_dates notes giving per-version deltas; known_limitations.methodological_limitation: 'Version 3.0.0 drops the Snellen visual acuity variables present in the prior version'; notes: 'there is no erratum'
sub_elements.quality_note: Version-to-version change is documented substantively — a named dropped variable, the cohort growth at each release, the withdrawal of 2.0.0 — and the CHANGELOG is shipped with the data.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The erratum position is an affirmative 'none exists' rather than an omission. The Snellen removal is corroborated in the visual_acuity_logmar variable note, so the change description is internally cross-checked.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence from E2.
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: 'approximately annually'; update_details: 'The dataset is not updated in place. New static versions are released with additional instances as more study participants complete the study visit, approximately once a year ... Further versions are expected, since enrolment is ongoing'
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the cadence and the update model (immutable versioned releases, not in-place revision) are stated, which is the information a reuser needs to plan citation and reproducibility.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The annual cadence is borne out by the actual release dates (May 2024, November 2024, November 2025) and is consistent with the ongoing enrolment described in collection_timeframes.

sub_elements.name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence from E2.
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources: nine entries mapping each raw source to its released form, e.g. Philips PageWriter TC30 .xml 'Converted to WFDB and distributed in the cardiac_ecg directory' and REDCap exports 'mapped one-to-one onto OMOP Common Data Model tables'; raw_sources explaining why raw data are withheld; related_datasets giving is_new_version_of lineage
sub_elements.quality_note: Provenance is traceable per modality from device export format through conversion to the released directory, and the retention and non-release policy for raw data is justified (unmapped terminologies, possible PHI in free text).
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Release-specific information is read from updates.update_details and notes as the instrument directs, and both carry actual release content rather than unrelated remarks. was_derived_from is unused, but raw_data_sources and related_datasets carry the derivation the sub-element asks for.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: four responses, including 'To create and publicly share a flagship, ethically sourced, multimodal dataset optimized for artificial intelligence and machine learning research into type 2 diabetes mellitus, including salutogenic pathways back to health'; addressing_gaps: three entries citing a meta-epidemiological review of 2000-2020 T2DM studies that found samples lacked racial and ethnic diversity
sub_elements.quality_note: Motivation is argued from named deficiencies in the prior literature and in existing data sources (claims data, EHRs), not asserted as generic importance.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The stated purposes align with the funding programme (NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Data Generation Project) and with the recruitment design in sampling_strategies, so motivation and method cohere.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: 'Downstream pseudotime manifold analysis: an approach used to predict disease trajectories by learning from complex, multimodal data collected from participants with differing disease severity' and multimodal AI/ML model development; other_tasks.task_details: 'The dataset is deliberately hypothesis agnostic; no specific labeling was performed'
sub_elements.quality_note: A specific named analytic strategy is given, and the deliberate absence of labels and of task-definition guidance is disclosed rather than left for the user to discover.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistent with instances.label=false and its label_description, and with known_limitations.temporal_limitation, which explains that pseudotime substitutes for repeated measures in a cross-sectional design.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health' with notes 'Award OT2OD032644 was made through the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program; the fiscal year 2022 award to the University of Washington was 5,026,499 US dollars, with a project period of 2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31'; grantor 'Research to Prevent Blindness'
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the agency and the funding mechanism are named, with award amount and project period, and the non-NIH funder is recorded with the source of the acknowledgement.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Funding logic satisfied: the NIH grantor is matched by structured grants, and Research to Prevent Blindness is recorded as an acknowledgement without a grant number, which the instrument treats as an alternative representation rather than a gap.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: funders.grants: 'OT2OD032644 — Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project' with id https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10471118; P30DK035816; UL1TR003096
sub_elements.quality_note: Three award numbers, one linked to its NIH RePORTER project record, with the publications in which each is acknowledged identified.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All three match NIH activity-code patterns and their institutes are coherent: OT2 (Other Transaction) with OD for a Common Fund programme, P30 with DK for a NIDDK centre, UL1 with TR for an NCATS CTSA. The RePORTER project id resolves to a plausible URL form.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators: 'AI-READI Consortium' with nine affiliations carrying ROR identifiers and principal_investigator 'Aaron Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648)'; maintainers acknowledging 'the Microsoft AI for Good Lab ... for supporting the cloud services needed for the project'; licence requirement to acknowledge licensor, source and funder
sub_elements.quality_note: Organizational creator, contributing institutions with persistent org identifiers, a named PI with ORCID, in-kind support and the citation obligation on reusers are all present.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: ORCID and ROR identifiers are well formed. The record explains that FAIRhub names a single organizational creator rather than individual authors, and discloses the unresolved conflict over the PI's institutional affiliation.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Collection identified (acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms populated) AND datasets-shared condition met on E2 evidence (distribution_formats, resolvable access page, is_shared true).
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: nine entries, e.g. 'A 12-lead electrocardiogram was recorded with a Philips PageWriter TC30 Cardiograph while the participant sat in a reclining chair or lay supine, with the chair position (0, 30, 60 or 90 degrees relative to supine) recorded'; the six named retinal imaging devices; Dexcom G6 at five-minute sampling for ten days; Garmin Vivosmart 5 at five-second sampling
sub_elements.quality_note: Settings are recorded at the level a replication would need — posture and chair angle, dilation status per device, wear duration, sampling frequency, wrist and dominance, sensor placement in the home.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Device names, sampling rates and durations agree with the variables entries and with the file_collections modality directories; the ten-day wear period matches the description.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same evidence as sub-element 1: collection identified and datasets shared.
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: four entries flagged was_directly_observed, was_reported_by_subjects and was_validated_verified, including 'cross-referencing entered medications against medications physically brought in or photographed by each study participant'; raw_data_sources naming each instrument and its export format
sub_elements.quality_note: Acquisition is classified by provenance type (observed, self-reported, verified, automatic) and each class is illustrated with the actual procedure, including a concrete verification step.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The provenance flags are used correctly and are consistent with raw_data_sources.source_type values (clinical device export, wearable device export, electronic data capture system, clinical laboratory report).

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Software-output condition met on E10/E2 evidence: external_resources references the code repository https://github.com/AI-READI, 'where the project publishes its guidelines and software for making data AI-ready', alongside https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi. Not asserted from E8's own fields.
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: four entries, e.g. 'Topcon Maestro2 and Triton data were exported in .fda format and converted to DICOM, and Heidelberg FLIO data were exported in .sdt format and converted to DICOM'; cleaning_strategies: three entries describing REDCap range flagging, the four classes of check (credibility, skip-pattern flow, fillable missing data, omission or duplication) and PI-approved editing; instances.label_description explaining why no labelling was done
sub_elements.quality_note: The pipeline is traceable per modality, the cleaning rules are specific and their governance is stated (edits only under site PI approval, no instances excluded at preprocessing), and the labelling position is explained rather than left blank.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Preprocessing claims match raw_data_sources conversions and the per-collection format standards. The evolution from 'custom and ad hoc handling for version 1.0.0' to automated processing for 2.0.0 and 3.0.0 is disclosed, which correctly signals that early and late data were not processed identically.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Element 8's datasets-shared condition is met (E2 distribution_formats and access page) and the release was demonstrably processed — preprocessing_strategies describes format conversions and terminology mapping — so the sub-element is scored rather than excused by the absence of a repository pointer.
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies name no tool: images 'required conversion to DICOM', Garmin '.FIT' data 'converted to the Open mHealth standard', ECG '.xml' data 'mapped to the WFDB format', and processing is described only as 'a combination of automated and custom processing'. The software that is named serves other roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application for capture; FAIRhub and Microsoft Azure for hosting; the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard (dqd_omop.json) for validation. external_resources points at https://github.com/AI-READI, the organization root.
sub_elements.quality_note: A reader cannot tell what software produced or transformed the distributed files. No slot — preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, imputation_protocols, machine_annotation_tools or external_resources — names a converter, mapper or pipeline, and none carries a version or repository tag.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Scored 0 under the processing-role threshold. The named software falls into excluded roles (a) capture and instrumentation (REDCap, MoCA Duo), (b) hosting and serving (FAIRhub, Azure) and (d) validation and quality assessment (OMOP DQD). The GitHub pointer identifies only the publishing organization, not a named piece of software, so under the threshold it neither earns nor forfeits the point.

sub_elements.name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on E2 evidence.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: docs.aireadi.org (CC-BY 4.0), the project site, the Zenodo community and GitHub organization, the Nature Metabolism comment (10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x), the BMJ Open protocol (10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449) and https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io; conforms_to describing CDS, WFDB, OMOP, DICOM, Open mHealth and NASA ESDS; missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy: 'No imputation of missing values is reported for the released dataset'
sub_elements.quality_note: Standards and external documentation are linked with an explanation of what each contributes, and the imputation question is answered affirmatively in the negative, with the one substitution actually performed (filling from elsewhere in the same record, under PI approval) described in cleaning_strategies.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Publication DOI prefixes are valid for their publishers; the CDS specification link corroborates the conforms_to claim rather than merely repeating it.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: six typed entries — representativeness, temporal, coverage, scope, methodological and integration — e.g. scope_limitation with scope_impact 'Fairness analyses stratified by sex or race/ethnicity cannot be performed on the public release alone, although the recommended splits were constructed to be balanced on those variables'
sub_elements.quality_note: Limitations are typed, each states its consequence for analysis, and several carry a recommended mitigation; the fairness-analysis consequence of the controlled-access split is exactly the kind of thing users otherwise discover too late.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Each limitation traces to something stated elsewhere: representativeness to sampling_strategies, coverage to missing_data_documentation, methodological to the visual_acuity_logmar variable note, scope to sensitive_elements.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: three entries with bias_type values selection_bias, sampling_bias and representation_bias, each with bias_description and mitigation_strategy, e.g. representation_bias noting the cohort 'does not include other races and ethnicities such as Pacific Islanders and Native Americans' and that the English-language requirement 'may also have created challenges in recruiting Hispanic and Asian participants'; affected_subsets on the sampling_bias entry
sub_elements.quality_note: Enumerated bias types with concrete mechanisms and paired mitigations, including a candid admission that interim releases are not balanced while enrolment continues.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The three bias_type values are drawn from the BiasTypeEnum vocabulary the sub-element asks for. Noted gap: future_use_impacts (rai:dataSocialImpact) is not populated, so anticipated downstream impact is carried only in prose elsewhere.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: six entries including 'Optomed Aurora fundus photographs are taken undilated with a handheld camera, so image quality varies from patient to patient and within the same patient' and 'Heidelberg Spectralis imaging is operated manually rather than automatically, so quality issues may arise that lead to skipping the modality and missing data'
sub_elements.quality_note: Each anomaly names the device or procedure that causes it and the analytic consequence, so a modeller can decide which files to filter rather than guessing.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The anomalies are physically plausible for the instruments named and are consistent with missing_data_documentation's causes and with the coverage limitation.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present: false with the explanation that 'sex, race and ethnicity, medications and protected health information have been removed' and that the separate controlled-access dataset does contain racial and ethnic origins, five-digit zip code, genetic sequencing data, past health records, medications and traffic and accident reports; content_warnings.content_warnings_present: false; confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present: false
sub_elements.quality_note: All three flags are accompanied by reasoning and by an explicit statement of what was moved to controlled access, which is what makes a 'false' informative rather than empty.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Registered as a low-severity semantic warning: 'no sensitive elements' is a strong claim for individual-level clinical, imaging and physiological data, defensible here only because of the documented removals, and the record does document them.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews[1]: 'Ethical, legal and social implications are stated to be considered at every stage of the project cycle, with guidance from bioethicists', with four named ELSI reviewers; ethical_reviews[2]: an eleven-member Community Advisory Board that 'evaluates the consent forms and research protocols, with its feedback considered in protocol and IRB modifications'; splits described as 'aimed at reducing disparities in models developed using the dataset when demographic labels are unavailable'; participant_privacy's account of AI-enabled re-identification as the motivation for watermarking and the licence
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethical review is documented as ongoing ELSI and community engagement rather than a single approval event, and downstream social impact is reasoned about concretely in two places: model disparity and AI-enabled re-identification.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Point earned on the ethical-review and impact-reasoning evidence, but the dedicated future_use_impacts slot is empty and notes record that no data protection impact analysis was conducted, so the social-impact half rests on prose scattered across other fields rather than a structured analysis.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on E2 evidence: distribution_formats populated, page and access page resolvable, third_party_sharing.is_shared true.
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: https://fairhub.io/; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; maintainers describing FAIRhub as 'a cloud-based data management, curation and sharing platform developed for this project on Microsoft Azure'
sub_elements.quality_note: The hosting platform is identified by resolvable URL and its nature and infrastructure are described, including the caveat that FAIRhub was in beta at version 2.0.0.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The publisher matches the DOI prefix registrant (10.60775, FAIRhub) and the landing page domain, a three-way agreement. The record also carries the notice that the repository 'is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives', which is material to platform stability.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Scored on the datasets-shared condition alone, as the instrument directs; no existing publication or citation count is required for applicability.
sub_elements.evidence: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3'; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; licence obligation to acknowledge licensor, source and funder in papers
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete formatted citation with creator, year, version, resource type, publisher and resolvable DOI, matched by the DOI field and reinforced by a contractual acknowledgement requirement.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Citation elements agree with creators, version, issued date and publisher. notes record zero citations at capture against 24,636 views, which is a usage fact and not a defect in the citation metadata.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence from E2.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: [CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS]; conforms_to prose mapping each standard to its datatype; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema
sub_elements.quality_note: Six community standards, each bound to the modality it governs, plus the datasheet schema itself; this is the strongest interoperability signal in the record.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: OMOP conformance is evidenced operationally by the Data Quality Dashboard file, and CDS conformance by the root metadata file list (dataset_description.json, participants.tsv and the rest), so the claims are checkable rather than nominal.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence from E2.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: https://docs.aireadi.org/ ('one version per dataset version ... covers citation, preliminary information including license and training prerequisites, the healthsheet and per-domain dataset documentation, AI-readiness considerations'), https://aireadi.org/ and /team and /goals/data-sharing, the Zenodo community, the GitHub organization, two publications and the CDS specification; page for the landing page
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation is versioned in step with the data, openly licensed CC-BY 4.0, and supplemented by project, code and publication venues; a newcomer has an obvious entry point at every level of depth.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All links are structurally valid and on plausible domains; the versioned documentation claim is corroborated by the per-version healthsheet URLs in version_access.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence from E2.
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: [{relationship_type: is_new_version_of, target_dataset: doi:10.60775/fairhub.2}, {relationship_type: is_new_version_of, target_dataset: doi:10.60775/fairhub.1}]
sub_elements.quality_note: Both predecessors are linked with an explicit relationship type and DOI targets, giving a machine-readable version chain.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship type is semantically correct for a versioned re-release and matches the narrative lineage in version_access and distribution_dates. Only version relationships are typed; the sibling Bridge2AI Data Generation Project datasets mentioned in the description are not linked.

strengths: Exceptional internal arithmetic consistency: file counts across the ten collections sum exactly to total_file_count, byte totals reconcile to within the unsized metadata files, and every cohort, split and stratum count sums correctly in both directions against the 2,280-participant total.

Source provenance is handled with unusual discipline: six substantive disagreements between FAIRhub, the RO-Crate, NIH RePORTER and the BMJ Open protocol are declared with their tier reasoning and left unresolved where the ranking cannot settle them, rather than silently merged.

Ethics documentation is complete and mutually consistent — IRB protocol number with approval date and published letter, reliance agreements for both satellite sites, named ELSI reviewers, a Community Advisory Board that reviewed the consent form, and consent recorded with type, scope, documentation and the honest limit of withdrawal.

Interoperability is grounded in six community standards bound to specific modalities (CDS, OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB, Open mHealth, NASA ESDS), each corroborated by artifacts in the release such as dqd_omop.json and the CDS root metadata files.

Collection methodology is documented at replication depth: named devices with settings, chair angles, dilation status, sampling frequencies and wear durations, alongside a data dictionary of roughly forty variables with units, measurement techniques and reference ranges.

Negative findings are recorded affirmatively rather than left blank — no imputation, no erratum, no labelling, no DPIA, no external audit, no vulnerable populations enrolled — each with the reasoning or eligibility rule that produces it.
weaknesses: No software that produced or transformed the released data is named anywhere: the .fda/.sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth, .xml to WFDB and REDCap to OMOP conversions are attributed only to 'a combination of automated and custom processing', and the GitHub link resolves to the organization root rather than a pipeline repository.

Deidentification is described two incompatible ways — 'NoDeIdentification, no identifiers were collected' against Safe Harbor removal of PHI plus an enumerated identifiers_removed list — and unlike the record's six declared source conflicts, this pair is left unreconciled.

The dedicated download_url slot is empty; the access endpoint https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access exists only inside data_governance.access_review_process prose, so machine consumers cannot resolve it.

No data protection impact assessment has been conducted, despite an assessed theoretical re-identification risk driven by AI inference, and no future_use_impacts entry records anticipated downstream social impact in structured form.

Character encoding is never stated for the CSV, JSON and Markdown components, and variable metadata uses local names without ontology identifiers such as LOINC, relying on OMOP conformance to supply standard concepts for the clinical tables only.

data_governance names a committee and an accountable organization but carries no committee_contact, leaving governance enquiries to be routed through contacts found in maintainers and ethical_reviews.
recommendations: Name the conversion and mapping software with versions and link the specific AI-READI repositories for each pipeline (.fda/.sdt to DICOM, .FIT and .csv to Open mHealth, .xml to WFDB, REDCap to OMOP), so the released files can be traced to the code that produced them.

Reconcile is_deidentified.method with participant_privacy.anonymization_method, stating both that no direct identifiers were captured and that a Safe Harbor review plus removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications preceded public release.
Populate download_url with https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access and data_governance.committee_contact with the Data Access Committee address.

Conduct and record a DPIA, or document in data_protection_impacts why one was judged unnecessary, and add future_use_impacts entries capturing anticipated downstream social impacts and the mitigations already described in splits, participant_privacy and the licence.

State character encoding for the text-based distributions and add ontology identifiers (for example LOINC codes) to the laboratory and vital-sign variables to extend interoperability beyond the OMOP-mapped clinical tables.

Consider carrying the raw source values for confidentiality classification ('HL7:2N (normal)', 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired') as structured fields beside the 'restricted' enum, so consumers filtering on the enum are not misled by the record's own mapping.
Name the conversion and mapping software with versions and link the specific AI-READI pipeline repositories rather than the GitHub organization root.
Reconcile the 'NoDeIdentification' method statement with the documented HIPAA Safe Harbor removal of PHI, sex, race/ethnicity and medications.
Populate download_url with the FAIRhub access endpoint and data_governance.committee_contact with a governance address.
Record a data protection impact assessment, or justify its absence, and add structured future_use_impacts entries for downstream social impact.
State character encoding for text distributions and add ontology identifiers to the variable metadata.

metadata.label: 2026-09-01_claude-opus-5-api-generic-v7_rep1
metadata.scoring_basis_note: No sub-element was excluded: the datasets-shared condition is met (distribution_formats, resolvable access page, is_shared true), the human-subjects condition is met (description names 2,280 participants; collection_mechanisms describes recruitment and consent), the governance condition is met (NIH GDS obligations, HIPAA status), data collection is identified, and external_resources references a code repository. Fixed and adjusted denominators are therefore both 50 and the two percentages coincide; comparability still requires matching evaluator model, instrument digest and excluded-item identities.
